title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Corinthians chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Corinthians Chapter 2.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling
I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified
I came not with excellency of speech or of wisdom
My speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man's wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: I came not with excellency of speech or of wisdom
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:1 states that Paul came not with excellency of speech or of wisdom, which is the first statement in the chapter.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 2, what did Paul declare to the brethren when he came to them?
options: The teachings of the princes of this world
questions.correctAnswer: The testimony of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:1 states that Paul declared unto them the testimony of God.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 2, what did Paul determine not to know among the brethren?
options: Anything save Jesus Christ, and him crucified
The laws of the Old Testament
questions.correctAnswer: Anything save Jesus Christ, and him crucified
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:2 states that Paul determined not to know any thing among them save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.

questions.question: How was Paul described as being with the brethren in 1 Corinthians 2?
options: In weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling
questions.correctAnswer: In weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:3 describes Paul as being with them in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling.

questions.question: What was Paul's speech and preaching NOT characterized by in 1 Corinthians 2?
options: Demonstration of the Spirit and of power
questions.correctAnswer: Enticing words of man's wisdom
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:4 states that Paul's speech and preaching was not with enticing words of man's wisdom.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 2, what was Paul's preaching a demonstration of?
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit and of power
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:4 states that Paul's preaching was a demonstration of the Spirit and of power.

questions.question: Why did Paul preach as he did, according to 1 Corinthians 2?
options: So that your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God
questions.correctAnswer: So that your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:5 explains that Paul preached so that their faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.

questions.question: Among whom does Paul say they speak wisdom in 1 Corinthians 2?
questions.correctAnswer: Them that are perfect
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:6 states that they speak wisdom among them that are perfect.

questions.question: What type of wisdom does Paul say they do NOT speak in 1 Corinthians 2?
options: The wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world
The wisdom given by the Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: The wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:6 clarifies that the wisdom spoken is not of this world, nor of the princes of this world.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 2, how does Paul describe the words of man's wisdom?
questions.correctAnswer: Enticing words
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:4 describes words of man's wisdom as enticing, which Paul did not use in his preaching.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 2, what should the faith of the brethren stand in?
questions.correctAnswer: The power of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:5 states that faith should stand in the power of God, not in the wisdom of men.

questions.question: True or False: Paul came to the brethren with excellency of speech and wisdom according to 1 Corinthians 2.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:1 explicitly states Paul did not come with excellency of speech or of wisdom.

questions.question: True or False: Paul's determination was to know nothing among the brethren except Jesus Christ and him crucified.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:2 states Paul determined not to know anything among them save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.

questions.question: True or False: Paul's speech and preaching was a demonstration of the Spirit and of power.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:4 states that Paul's speech and preaching was in demonstration of the Spirit and of power.

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Corinthians 2, Paul says he used enticing words of man's wisdom to persuade the brethren.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:4 clearly states Paul did not use enticing words of man's wisdom in his preaching.

medium.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Corinthians Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What is described as the wisdom of God in 1 Corinthians 2:7?
questions.correctAnswer: A mystery
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:7 states that 'we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery,' indicating that the wisdom is not fully understood by all.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 2:8 indicate about the princes of this world?
options: They understood the wisdom of God
They did not know the wisdom of God
They were wise in their own ways
They were unaware of God's plans
questions.correctAnswer: They did not know the wisdom of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:8 explains that 'none of the princes of this world knew' the wisdom of God.

questions.question: What things does 1 Corinthians 2:9 say eye has not seen or ear heard?
options: The things prepared for those who love God
questions.correctAnswer: The things prepared for those who love God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:9 reveals that 'Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.'

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 2:10, who reveals the deep things of God?
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:10 states, 'But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit,' indicating the role of the Spirit in revealing God's truths.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 2:11 say about knowing the things of God?
options: Only the Spirit of God knows them
Any wise man can know them
questions.correctAnswer: Only the Spirit of God knows them
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:11 states, 'for the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God,' emphasizing that only the Spirit comprehends divine truths.

questions.question: What spirit have we received according to 1 Corinthians 2:12?
questions.correctAnswer: The spirit of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:12 indicates, 'Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God,' highlighting our connection to divine understanding.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 2:1 say about Paul's approach when he came to the Corinthians?
questions.correctAnswer: In fear and trembling
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:3 states, 'And I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling,' illustrating Paul's humble approach.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 2:5, where should your faith stand?
questions.correctAnswer: In the power of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:5 emphasizes that 'your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.'

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 2:4 say about Paul's preaching?
options: It was in demonstration of the Spirit and of power
questions.correctAnswer: It was in demonstration of the Spirit and of power
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:4 states, 'And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man's wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power,' focusing on divine authority.

questions.question: What is the significance of the hidden wisdom mentioned in 1 Corinthians 2:7?
options: It is ordained for our glory
questions.correctAnswer: It is ordained for our glory
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:7 mentions that the hidden wisdom was 'ordained before the world unto our glory,' indicating its purpose and significance.

questions.question: How does the context of 1 Corinthians 2:1-5 relate to the power of God?
options: It highlights the weakness of believers
It contrasts divine power with human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: It contrasts divine power with human wisdom
questions.explanation: The verses from 1 Corinthians 2:1-5 collectively show how Paul did not rely on human wisdom but emphasized 'the power of God.'

questions.question: The statement 'Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard...' refers to what in 1 Corinthians 2:9?
options: The things prepared for those who love God
questions.correctAnswer: The things prepared for those who love God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:9 reveals that 'the things which God hath prepared for them that love him' are beyond human perception.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 2:10, God has revealed all things to all men.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:10 clarifies that God reveals things 'unto us by his Spirit,' indicating that not all men receive this revelation.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 2:12 teaches that we have received the spirit of the world.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:12 states that we have received 'the spirit which is of God,' not the spirit of the world.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 2:8 implies that if the princes of this world had known God's wisdom, they would not have crucified Jesus.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:8 indicates that 'had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory,' highlighting their ignorance of divine wisdom.

hard.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Corinthians Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 2:13, how do we speak the things taught by the Holy Ghost?
options: In the words which man's wisdom teacheth
In the words which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual
In the wisdom of the princes of this world
In enticing words of man's wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: In the words which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:13 states that we speak not in the words which man's wisdom teacheth, but those which the Holy Ghost teacheth, comparing spiritual things with spiritual.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 2:14 say about the natural man's ability to receive the things of the Spirit of God?
options: He receiveth and understands them fully
He receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God; they are foolishness unto him
He can know them because they are plainly seen
questions.correctAnswer: He receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God; they are foolishness unto him
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:14 clearly states that the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God because they are foolishness unto him and he cannot know them since they are spiritually discerned.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 2:15, who is able to judge all things?
questions.correctAnswer: He that is spiritual
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:15 explains that he that is spiritual judgeth all things, yet he himself is judged of no man.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 2:16, who has the mind that we have?
questions.correctAnswer: Christ
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:16 states that we have the mind of Christ, referring to the understanding and wisdom given to believers.

questions.question: What does Paul say he did not come with when he first came to the Corinthians in 1 Corinthians 2:1?
options: Excellency of speech or of wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Excellency of speech or of wisdom
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:1 states that Paul did not come with excellency of speech or of wisdom, but declaring the testimony of God.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 2:2, what did Paul determine not to know among the Corinthians?
options: Any thing save Jesus Christ, and him crucified
questions.correctAnswer: Any thing save Jesus Christ, and him crucified
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:2 reveals Paul's determination to know nothing among the Corinthians except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'pneuma' (πνεῦμα) in 1 Corinthians 2:13 primarily mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Spirit or breath
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'pneuma' (πνεῦμα) used in 1 Corinthians 2:13 means 'spirit' or 'breath,' referring to the Holy Spirit teaching spiritual things.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 1 Corinthians 2:13's phrase 'comparing spiritual things with spiritual'?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:13 uses parallelism by balancing 'spiritual things' with 'spiritual' to emphasize the spiritual nature of the teaching.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of 'Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard' in 1 Corinthians 2:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 64:4
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:9 quotes Isaiah 64:4 about the unseen and unheard things God has prepared for those who love Him.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of spiritual discernment and the natural man in 1 Corinthians 2:14?
questions.correctAnswer: John 3:6
questions.explanation: John 3:6 states that that which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit, echoing the natural man’s inability to receive spiritual things as in 1 Corinthians 2:14.

questions.question: What comes immediately before 1 Corinthians 2:13 in the chapter?
options: We have received the spirit which is of God
The natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit
Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard
questions.correctAnswer: We have received the spirit which is of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:12 precedes 2:13 and states that we have received the spirit which is of God, setting the context for speaking spiritual things in 2:13.

questions.question: What is the typological significance of 'Jesus Christ, and him crucified' in 1 Corinthians 2:2?
options: Christ as the fulfillment of the Old Testament sacrificial system
questions.correctAnswer: Christ as the fulfillment of the Old Testament sacrificial system
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:2's focus on Jesus Christ crucified typologically fulfills the Old Testament sacrificial system as the ultimate sacrifice for sin.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 2:10 use inclusio as a literary device in the context of revelation?
options: By framing the 'deep things of God' between 'God hath revealed' and 'the Spirit searcheth all things'
By repeating the phrase 'deep things' multiple times
By contrasting natural and spiritual knowledge
questions.correctAnswer: By framing the 'deep things of God' between 'God hath revealed' and 'the Spirit searcheth all things'
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:10 uses inclusio by placing 'deep things of God' between the statement that God hath revealed them and that the Spirit searcheth all things, creating literary framing.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 2:15, the spiritual man is judged by all men.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:15 states that he that is spiritual judgeth all things, yet he himself is judged of no man, so the spiritual man is not judged by others.

questions.question: True or False: The natural man can understand spiritual things because they are discerned naturally according to 1 Corinthians 2:14.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:14 declares the natural man cannot know the things of the Spirit of God because they are spiritually discerned, not naturally.

theological.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Corinthians Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 2:2 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is centered exclusively on Jesus Christ and his crucifixion
Salvation is attained through human wisdom and eloquent speech
Salvation is a result of human effort and moral achievement
Salvation depends on adherence to the Mosaic Law
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is centered exclusively on Jesus Christ and his crucifixion
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:2 states Paul determined to know nothing among them except Jesus Christ and him crucified, emphasizing salvation's exclusive foundation in Christ's atoning death.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the Holy Spirit is taught in 1 Corinthians 2:10?
options: The Spirit reveals God's hidden wisdom and searches the deep things of God
The Spirit only inspires the writing of Scripture but does not reveal mysteries
The Spirit is limited in knowledge and cannot reveal divine truths
The Spirit works primarily through human reason and philosophy
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit reveals God's hidden wisdom and searches the deep things of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:10 explains that God reveals hidden wisdom through His Spirit who searches all things, including the deep things of God, signifying the Spirit's revelatory role.

questions.question: What doctrine about human nature and spiritual discernment is taught in 1 Corinthians 2:14?
options: The natural man cannot receive or understand the things of the Spirit because they are spiritually discerned
All humans can understand spiritual truths through natural reason alone
Spiritual truths are accessible primarily through cultural traditions
The natural man can discern spiritual matters without divine aid
questions.correctAnswer: The natural man cannot receive or understand the things of the Spirit because they are spiritually discerned
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:14 teaches that the natural man does not accept the things of the Spirit of God because they are foolishness to him and cannot be understood apart from spiritual discernment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 2:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:7 speaks of God's wisdom ordained before the world unto our glory, demonstrating God's sovereign plan in revealing hidden wisdom according to His divine will.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 1 Corinthians 2:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:11 emphasizes that only the Spirit of God knows the things of God, highlighting God's attribute of omniscience—His perfect knowledge.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 2:5 prepare the narrative arc of faith in the New Testament?
options: It emphasizes faith resting on God's power rather than human wisdom, preparing for the theme of divine empowerment in faith
It promotes reliance on human philosophy for salvation
It teaches that faith is irrelevant to salvation
It suggests that wisdom of men is superior to divine power
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes faith resting on God's power rather than human wisdom, preparing for the theme of divine empowerment in faith
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:5 states faith should stand in the power of God, not human wisdom, which aligns with New Testament themes of faith empowered by God rather than human intellect.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is made in 1 Corinthians 2:8?
options: The rulers of this world crucified the Lord of glory because they did not understand God's hidden wisdom
The rulers of this world fully comprehended Jesus’ mission and accepted it
The crucifixion was a mistake unrelated to divine wisdom
The crucifixion was a political act without spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: The rulers of this world crucified the Lord of glory because they did not understand God's hidden wisdom
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:8 explains that the princes of this world did not know God's wisdom, or they would not have crucified the Lord of glory, showing the spiritual blindness at the crucifixion event.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 12 and 13 teach about spiritual knowledge?
options: Believers receive the Spirit of God to know spiritual truths, and they communicate these truths in Spirit-taught words
Spiritual truths are learned through human wisdom and worldly philosophy
The Spirit of the world is sufficient to understand God's mysteries
Spiritual knowledge is acquired primarily through academic study
questions.correctAnswer: Believers receive the Spirit of God to know spiritual truths, and they communicate these truths in Spirit-taught words
questions.explanation: Verses 12 and 13 teach that believers have received the Spirit of God to know what God freely gives and speak these things not with human wisdom but by the Holy Spirit’s teaching.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 9 and 16 teach about the believer's hope and mind?
options: God has prepared unimaginable blessings for those who love Him, and believers have the mind of Christ to understand His will
Human senses and reasoning can fully grasp divine realities without spiritual transformation
The things God prepared are known through philosophical speculation alone
Believers are left to discern God's mind apart from Christ's guidance
questions.correctAnswer: God has prepared unimaginable blessings for those who love Him, and believers have the mind of Christ to understand His will
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 16 highlight that what God has prepared exceeds human perception and that believers possess the mind of Christ, enabling spiritual insight into God's plans.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 4 and 5 teach about the basis of faith?
options: Preaching is empowered by the Spirit and power so that faith rests on God’s power, not human wisdom
Faith is founded primarily on persuasive human reasoning and eloquence
Faith depends on the cultural acceptance of the message
Human wisdom and power are sufficient for genuine faith
questions.correctAnswer: Preaching is empowered by the Spirit and power so that faith rests on God’s power, not human wisdom
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 teach that Paul's preaching was demonstrated by the Spirit and power so that faith would rest on God's power, not on human wisdom or eloquent speech.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the message of 1 Corinthians 2:6-8 is outdated and irrelevant because it relies on mysterious wisdom. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches that God's wisdom is a hidden, divine mystery that worldly rulers failed to understand, which led to the crucifixion of Christ
It claims that worldly wisdom is superior and more reliable than divine wisdom
It suggests that the crucifixion was a misunderstanding and does not relate to God's wisdom
It states that only worldly rulers have true wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that God's wisdom is a hidden, divine mystery that worldly rulers failed to understand, which led to the crucifixion of Christ
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:6-8 explains that the wisdom God speaks is a hidden mystery not known by worldly rulers, who crucified Christ due to their ignorance of this divine plan.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 2:15 teach about the spiritual person’s role and judgment?
options: The spiritual person judges all things but is not judged by others
The spiritual person is subject to judgment by worldly authorities but cannot judge
The spiritual person is ignorant of spiritual matters
The spiritual person judges himself only and is judged by all
questions.correctAnswer: The spiritual person judges all things but is not judged by others
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:15 states that the spiritual person discerns all things but himself is not subject to judgment by others, highlighting spiritual discernment and immunity from human judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly highlighted in 1 Corinthians 2:16?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:16 references knowing the mind of the Lord, which relates to God's omniscience—His all-knowing nature, and believers having the mind of Christ.

questions.question: What theological synthesis can be drawn from 1 Corinthians 2:1 and 1 Corinthians 2:3 about Paul’s approach to ministry?
options: Paul ministers in weakness and fear, not relying on human wisdom or eloquence
Paul relies on rhetorical skill and confidence to persuade his audience
Paul emphasizes human wisdom over the Spirit’s power
Paul’s ministry is characterized by boldness and eloquent speech
questions.correctAnswer: Paul ministers in weakness and fear, not relying on human wisdom or eloquence
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 3 show Paul came without excellence of speech but with weakness, fear, and trembling, indicating reliance on God rather than human ability in ministry.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does 1 Corinthians 2:13 make in the broader New Testament context?
options: It connects the teaching of spiritual truths through the Holy Spirit to the ongoing apostolic witness and preaching
It teaches that spiritual truths should be communicated only through written Scripture
It advocates for the use of human philosophy to explain spiritual matters
It denies the need for the Spirit in teaching spiritual truths
questions.correctAnswer: It connects the teaching of spiritual truths through the Holy Spirit to the ongoing apostolic witness and preaching
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:13 emphasizes that spiritual truths are taught by the Holy Spirit, aligning with the New Testament theme of Spirit-empowered apostolic preaching.
